newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP approves economy-based forest policy.
newsitem.headline: EP approves economy-based forest policy.

text.p: The European Parliament approved on Thursday a report on European Union forestry policy which emphasises the economic value of forests.

Green MEPs attempted to amend the report to put more accent on the need to manage EU forests sustainably if their natural resources are to survive, but they failed to win the absolute majority necessary to push their amendments through.
Rapporteur David Thomas, a British Socialist, told Reuters after the vote he was relieved the controversial report had finally been adopted.
It has taken Thomas two years to find a formula that could win the support of a majority of MEPs.

Stefan Leiner of the World Wide Fund for Nature told Reuters the WWF was disappointed with the report, which is intended as a contribution to a proposal for an EU forest strategy which the European Commission has pledged to produce within two years.
"The report fails to put the environmental, social and economic aspects of forests on an equal footing," Leiner said.
